docs.title: Invoices and bills: the invoice line sync and the tax computation

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

An invoice is an account.move whose move_type is out_invoice (customer invoice), out_refund (customer credit note), in_invoice (vendor bill) or in_refund (vendor credit note). Code: erp_addon_account::invoice and erp_addon_account::tax::compute.

| Model | Field | Meaning | |---|---|---| | account.move | invoice_date | invoice or bill date | | account.move | invoice_date_due | due date: the last instalment of the payment terms, else the date set by hand, else the invoice date (see [Payment terms](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/account-payment-terms.md)) | | account.move | invoice_line_ids | the line_ids whose display_type is product, section, subsection or note (a one2many with a domain on the same inverse) | | account.move | amount_untaxed, amount_tax, amount_total | totals in the document currency, positive on an ordinary invoice | | account.move | amount_residual, payment_state | the total and not_paid until payments are available | | account.move.line | product_id, product_uom_id, quantity, price_unit, discount, tax_ids | what the user edits on a product line | | account.move.line | tax_repartition_line_id, tax_line_id | on a tax line: the repartition line it was made from, and its tax | | account.move.line | price_subtotal, price_total | the line amount without and with taxes | display_type gained tax and payment_term (the receivable or payable line). The totals, the amount due and the payment status (moves::SYNC_OWNED_FIELDS) are written by the line sync only. A caller value for one of them is refused with a UserError that names the field, on create and on write, on a draft as well as on a posted document, and so is the context key default_<field> for one of them: change the lines, the totals follow. A write on the item model itself (account.move.line) does not run the sync; posting runs it once more for every draft invoice before its checks, so a posted invoice always carries the figures of its lines.

invoice::sync_lines(tx, env, move_ids) runs after every create of an entry and after every write of a draft invoice that changes its lines, partner, currency, type, journal, company or dates. For each draft invoice it: 1. computes the taxes of each product line (tax::compute::compute) and writes the line's amount_currency (subtotal times invoice::direction_sign: credit on a customer invoice, debit on a vendor bill, reversed on credit notes), price_subtotal and price_total; 2. splits each tax amount over the tax's tax repartition lines of the document kind (invoice or refund) and keeps one tax line per repartition line and account (the repartition line's account, else the product line's account); a zero amount makes no line; 3. keeps the receivable (customer documents) or payable (vendor documents) lines that balance the entry in both currencies: one line, due at the due date, or one per instalment of the payment terms ([Payment terms](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/account-payment-terms.md)). Its account is chosen as described under [The receivable or payable account](#the-receivable-or-payable-account); 4. writes the header totals, the amount due and the payment state when one of them changed. New product lines without an account take the journal's default account; without one the save is refused (product accounts are not available yet). When creating a draft without a journal, the addon searches sale or purchase journals for the company and its parents in journal order. If the draft supplies a foreign currency_id (directly or through default_currency_id), a journal in that currency takes priority. Without a match it takes the first eligible journal and keeps the requested document currency. A currency change moves every product, tax and receivable or payable line to the new currency: the amount in currency is written with it, so the balance is converted at the new currency's rate on the accounting date (a currency without a rate is refused naming it). The balances of a draft invoice in another currency than its company's are converted at the entry's accounting date. When that date changes on the draft, the write runs invoice::sync_lines_redated(tx, env, move_ids), which converts the product, tax and receivable or payable balances again at the new date; the amounts in currency do not change. The re-dating at posting (an accounting date moved by a lock date) keeps the balances as they are. What the sync costs: reads are one query per field for all the invoices together; new lines are created in one call and stale lines deleted in one call; each changed line is written with its own write (a bulk-write API is a follow-up) and the header once per invoice whose totals changed. Lines and headers that already match are not written. A cell of an unexpected kind or a short column in one of these reads is refused naming the field; it is never read as an empty value.

The receivable line of a customer document takes an account of type asset_receivable, the payable line of a vendor document one of type liability_payable: 1. a line that already has an account of the right type keeps it; 2. otherwise the candidates are the accounts of that type shared with the invoice's company or one of its parent companies (a branch uses the accounts of its parent); 3. no candidate: the save is refused naming what to create; 4. one candidate: it is used; 5. several candidates: the one whose code is entered in the company's Accounting settings, block "Invoices", is used. The settings are account.invoice_receivable_account_code ("Invoices: receivable account of customer invoices (account code)") and account.invoice_payable_account_code ("Invoices: payable account of vendor bills (account code)"), one value per company, empty by default, written by accounting managers. With an empty setting or a code that none of the candidates has, the save is refused listing the candidate codes and naming the setting. An account is never picked by its position among several.

tax::compute::compute(&BaseLine) is pure (no database). It takes the unit price, quantity, discount, the line's TaxDefs and the document currency increment, and returns the subtotal, the total and one TaxAmount (base and amount) per evaluated tax. Supported: percent, fixed and division taxes, groups of taxes (their children are evaluated at the group's place), price-included taxes, taxes that affect the base of later ones, ordering by sequence then id, and rounding per line (half away from zero, ADR 0046). Python code taxes and reverse charge are refused with a message that they are not available yet. Groups are supported by the module but the database has no child taxes yet, so a group tax on a line is refused with a message saying so. The company has no "round globally" choice yet.

The posting service calls invoice::post::check_postable(tx, env, move_ids) and invoice::post::before_post(tx, env, move_ids); both do nothing for plain journal entries. - check_postable refuses, in one error listing every problem: an invoice without customer or vendor, without a product line, with a negative total, or a vendor document without its bill date. - before_post gives customer documents without an invoice date today's date (in the user's timezone); vendor documents keep the date printed by the vendor.

Receipts, early payment discount and cash rounding of payment terms, product accounts, fiscal positions, cash rounding, payments, the overdue search filter (the client cannot compare with today's date in a domain yet), unit conversion of the product price.

docs.title: Ledger configuration models of the account addon

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

Source: addons/account/src/ledger/ (accounts) and addons/account/src/journal/ (journals). Spec: docs/specs/accounting/ledger-config.md (ACCLED). Plain company accounting configuration lives in addons/account/src/company/.

| Model | Table | What it is | |---|---|---| | account.account | account_account | An account of the chart. Shared by the companies of company_ids. | | account.account.tag | account_account_tag | A reporting tag (accounts, taxes, products). Unique per name, applicability and country. | | account.root | account_root | The first two characters of a code, as a small tree (10 below 1). | | account.code.mapping | account_account_code | The code of an account in one root company. | | account.journal | account_journal | A journal of one company: type, code, default and special accounts, numbering declaration. | | account.journal.group | account_journal_group | A ledger: a named group of journals, one list for the database. |

Odoo keeps the code in a company-dependent JSON column and checks uniqueness with a Python search. Here the code is a row of account_account_code per account and **root** company (ADR 0048 D3): - UNIQUE (company_id, code): two accounts of one company tree cannot share a code, and the database says so (SPEC-ACCLED-017, Parity: divergent, ADR 0048 D3). Sibling company trees have different roots and may reuse a code. - UNIQUE (account_id, company_id): one code per account and tree. - A branch company reads and writes its root's code (SPEC-ACCLED-029, 030). A mapping row for a branch is refused. account.account.code is a computed, writable field over that table in the environment's company (depends_context = ["company"]). Writing it stores the code for the root of the active company, or removes the row when the value is empty. account.root rows are created when a code is stored and never removed; each missing prefix is one insert-if-absent on the _name_uniq key (the ORM upsert with nothing to update), so two transactions that first use the same prefix both succeed (the later one is retried by Orm::run after a serialization failure). A code given at **create** is stored for the root of the active company when the account belongs to that tree, else for the root of the account's first company that is also a company of the caller (lowest company id), as the reference creates under the caller's allowed companies (odoo/addons/account/models/account_account.py:1023-1025, :1042-1043). A caller with companies [A, C] creating an account of [B, C] stores the code in C's tree, never B's; when the account belongs to none of the caller's companies the create is a Validation error. Only superuser mode takes the lowest company id of the account. An account created from company A with company_ids = [B] in superuser mode therefore reads its code in B and uses no code of A's tree. A code value that is neither absent, null nor text is a Validation error. The account_id and company_id of an account.code.mapping row are set at create only; account_id is readonly (the one2many sets it) but company_id is not, so the "Codes by company" list can send it for a new row. A write that gives either a value other than the stored one is a Validation error; naming the stored value passes. Only code is written. // the code of an account as seen from a company let in_company = tx.env().with_company(company)?.records("account.account")?; let account = in_company.browse([id])?; let code = account.cell(&mut tx, "code").await?; // written from a branch: changes the root's code for the whole tree account.write(&mut tx, RawVals::new().set_cell("code", Cell::Str("180002".into()))).await?; Reading code without an active company in the context is a Validation error, not an empty value. A create may carry code_mapping_ids create commands. The x2many values of a create are written in field order, and the company check of a row reads the account's company_ids, so code_mapping_ids is declared after company_ids in the model; keep that order in any extension that adds company-checked one2many fields to an account. A row for a company outside company_ids is refused by the company check, never skipped.

account_type has the 19 types of the reference. internal_group (the part before the first underscore) and include_initial_balance are stored computed fields; reconcile is a stored computed field that the type forces for receivable, payable, bank and cash, credit card, off-balance and the income, expense and equity groups, and leaves to the user for the other asset and liability types. Constraints: receivable and payable must reconcile; off-balance must not and cannot carry default taxes; a bank or cash account has one company; every account has at least one company; a code uses letters, digits, dots and dashes. An account created without company_ids gets the active company.

Another addon adds fields with #[extend(AccountAccount, addon = "...")] (or AccountJournal) as for any model (see [Extending other addons](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/cross-addon-extension.md)). The _check_* constraints compose through the usual override chain. The move slice adds the journal item guards.

account.journal has the six types of the reference (sale, purchase, cash, bank, credit, general), a company (the active company when none is given, also for an empty value; a company id given as an integer is accepted, any other value is refused; branches use their parent's journals: company access ancestor, company match parent_of) and a code unique per company (UNIQUE (company_id, code)). | Rule | When | Message names | |---|---|---| | A journal without code gets <prefix><n>, the first n free in the company and its parents (archived journals included) and in the same create call; outside superuser mode only in a company the caller may create journals in (an active company or a parent of one), else Access before any code is read | create | the code length setting when no code fits | | Two creates at the same time that propose the same code: the first wins, the second fails with a Conflict (when the call typed no code; a typed duplicate keeps the unique-key refusal) | create | "save again" | | The code has 1 to account.journal_code_max_length characters, without a space at its start or end | create, write of code | the setting | | A default account the caller cannot read is refused before its type is read, with the same sentence whatever that type is | create, write of type or default_account_id; account type change | the account by its id and the journal type | | A sale or purchase journal never defaults to a receivable or payable account | same | the reference's two messages | | The default account's type is in account.journal_account_types_<type> | same | the type and the setting | | Journal and default account agree on the foreign currency (an account without currency fits) | journal create, journal write of currency_id or default_account_id, account write of currency_id | journal and account names | | Writing a currency on a bank, cash or credit card journal copies it onto its default account | journal write | | | A bank, cash or credit card journal has a default account (until the account is created for it) | create, write of type or default_account_id | the company accounting fields | | An account keeps the companies of the journals using it as default, suspense, profit or loss account (the journal's company or one of its parents) | account write of company_ids | account, field and journal (a journal the caller cannot read by its id) | | An account used by a journal in one of those four fields cannot be deleted; a ledger used by a journal cannot be deleted | delete | the journal model | check_currency_consistency(tx, env, journals, accounts), check_accounts_as_default(tx, env, accounts) and check_journal_companies(tx, env, accounts) in erp_addon_account::journal are the shared checks; the account constraints call them. A refusal names a journal or an account only when the caller may read it, otherwise by id, also when the caller may not read the model at all.

The journal stores what the reference reads back from the previous entry name (ADR 0048 D2.2): sequence_reset (never, year, month, year_range, year_range_month), sequence_padding (1 to 64 digits), refund_sequence and payment_sequence. They default from the type (sales and liquidity journals: yearly, five digits; the others: monthly, four digits; credit notes apart for sale and purchase, payments apart for bank, cash and credit card); values given at create are kept. The restart rule and the digits are set only at create: a later type change keeps them, while the two separate-chain flags follow the type. The database refuses digits outside 1 to 64. The numbering service reads the declaration through JournalSequence, which only JournalSequence::of makes: use erp_addon_account::journal::{AccountJournal, JournalSequence}; let journal = tx.env().model::<AccountJournal>()?.browse(vec![journal_id])?; let sequence = JournalSequence::of(tx, &journal).await?; // a refund without its own chain is numbered in the document chain let (kind, pattern) = sequence.pattern("refund")?; // ("refund", RINV1/2026/00001 ...) A journal whose code and numbering cannot make a valid pattern is refused when it is saved, never at posting. account.sequence.chain.journal_id is still an integer column; it becomes a many2one to account.journal with the journal entry work, which also rewrites the numbering tests that use free journal ids.

Declared settings of the accounting app (database scope, block "Journals"; read: account.group_account_readonly, write: account.group_account_manager): | Setting | Default | Bounds | |---|---|---| | account.journal_code_max_length | 16 | 1 to 32 characters | | account.journal_code_prefix_<type> | INV, BILL, CSH, BNK, CCD, MISC | one word, at most 16 bytes | | account.journal_account_types_<type> | the reference's default-account domain per type | a comma list of known account types, at most 512 bytes | JournalSettings::read(tx) reads them all in one statement with the framework's rights. A value of the wrong kind or outside its bounds is refused naming the key and its bounds; an empty list of account types is refused. A changed setting applies to the next create or write of a journal or account: existing journals are not checked again.

account.journal.dashboard_card is a computed, non-stored text field holding the card contract v1 as JSON (buttons, stats, chart; addons/account/src/journal/dashboard.rs). The kanban account.account_journal_dashboard_kanban_view (action account.open_account_journal_dashboard_kanban, menu Accounting > Dashboard) shows it with the dashboard_card widget for the journals with show_on_dashboard. Each card element and its reference counterpart: docs/design/accounting-dashboard-matrix.md. - One computation serves every requested journal with a fixed set of grouped reads (_read_group on account.move and account.move.line), never one query per journal; the reads run with the reader's rights, so record rules and the company scope apply. A reader without accounting access gets the access error. - Every stat and chart is always shown; one that counts nothing shows zero in the neutral tone (the reference hides such a row and draws sample bars on an empty journal). - Sales and purchases: button New Invoice or New Bill; "Drafts", "Unpaid" (sales) or "To pay" (purchases) and "Late" (posted, due before today in the user's time zone) from the lines on receivable and payable accounts (balance, purchases shown positive, date_maturity); a bar chart of the posted invoiced (billed) amount per month. Each figure opens account.action_move_out_documents (sales) or account.action_move_in_documents (purchases): the invoice list without a document-type domain, so it shows every document the figure counts. - Bank, cash and credit card: no button; "Balance", the posted balance of the default account in the journal's company, linking to its journal items; "Transactions", the number of the journal's plain entries, opening them (until statements exist); a line chart of the running balance per day. - Miscellaneous: button New Entry; "Drafts"; no chart. - Until reconciliation exists, "open" means posted: the residual replaces the balance when it arrives. - Labels are in the source language (dashboard::labels): the addon has no server-side code-text translation yet. | Setting (database scope, block "Dashboard") | Default | Bounds | |---|---|---| | account.dashboard_graph_months | 13 (the current month and the twelve before) | 1 to 36 months | | account.dashboard_balance_days | 30 | 7 to 64 days (one chart point per day; a card shows at most 64) |

account.journal.group (a "ledger"): name unique in the database ("Another ledger already has this name."), sequence (default 10) and included_journal_ids, the journals whose journal_group_id points to it, archived ones included. Like the reference it has no company. A ledger that a journal uses, archived journals included, cannot be deleted (journal_group_id is restrict): the reference empties the ledger of the journals of every company.

- Default data: the three master tags (account_tag_operating, account_tag_financing, account_tag_investing), which cannot be deleted. The reference ships no accounts, roots or code mappings: accounts come from a chart template (the chart-template slice) and roots follow the codes (SPEC-ACCLED-053; tested in crates/erp-cli/tests/account_install.rs). No journals or journal groups either: the reference creates the standard journals when a chart is loaded into a company, and that list belongs to the chart-loading slice (SPEC-ACCLED-102). - Groups (security/account_security.xml): group_account_readonly, group_account_user, group_account_manager. the security-data slice extends them. - Company rule: generated from company_access (accounts by company_ids and ancestors, code rows and journals by company_id and ancestors). Journal groups have no company. - Access: journals and journal groups are read by group_account_readonly and managed by group_account_manager. - Menus: Accounting > Configuration > Chart of Accounts, Account Tags, Journals (managers), Ledgers.

The account addon extends res.company with ordinary account references for transfers, bank suspense, cash differences, cash discounts, exchange differences, PoS receivables and accruals, and journal references for exchange differences and automatic entries. References start unset, use restrictive foreign keys and obey the framework's company consistency rules. An account or journal of an unrelated company cannot be assigned, including through elevated ORM operations; permitted parent-company targets remain usable by a branch. Removing a selected account's company membership or moving a selected journal is refused when it would strand a configuration reference. The refusal names no hidden company. Failed native writes still require an enclosing savepoint or transaction rollback, as other ORM writes do. These fields are ordinary company columns, independent of the typed company-dependent account mappings. Company fields also store bank, cash and transfer account-code prefixes (empty or up to 64 ASCII letters, digits, dots and dashes), tax rounding (round_globally by default or round_per_line), Anglo-Saxon accounting (false by default), and whether a chart is expected (true). Prefix and option writes configure future consumers; they do not create or rename accounts or post entries. The chart identifier is read-only until chart activation is available. The company form cannot activate or clear an installed chart. **Settings > Accounting > Company accounting** opens the explicitly selected company's configuration form. This is a scoped Settings link, not a second copy of the relational values in scalar settings storage. Existing company-management permissions apply; accounting-manager membership alone grants no company writes. Configuration writes check company scope before reading target details. Existing fiscal-year settings and lock-date policy remain separate; the form does not offer a generic lock-date editor.

Upgrade account before serving a binary that declares the company configuration link: the upgrade installs its action and form along with the new columns. A missing link target is refused during Settings publication. Existing companies retain their tax, lock and accounting configuration on upgrade. No jurisdiction-specific accounts or journals are seeded by this extension; references remain empty until configured from the company's chart. Not available yet: automatic journal account creation, use of company suspense/cash-difference defaults by journals, prefix-driven renumbering, chart activation, and effective company-dependent receivable/payable/income/ expense/valuation defaults. These limitations are independent of saving the plain configuration fields.

| Case | Why | Slice | |---|---|---| | SPEC-ACCLED-007, 008, 019..026, 035, 038, 040, 041 | account type from the code, name_create, name search, copy, ordering by code, search with archived parents, placeholder code | follow-up slice of the ledger configuration models | | SPEC-ACCLED-014, 016, 036 | need journal items | the journal items | | SPEC-ACCLED-062, 063, 064 | journal company change and archive with entries | the journal items | | SPEC-ACCLED-057, 067 | effective company and category account defaults | account mapping runtime | | SPEC-ACCLED-058 | liquidity accounts created from prefixes; company suspense and cash-difference defaults consumed by journals | liquidity defaults and prefix lifecycle | | SPEC-ACCLED-060, 066 | code from the name on import, payment reference from the code | import slice, invoices slice | | SPEC-ACCLED-042..050 | balances, merge wizard | the account wizards slice, reports | | mapped company defaults | typed company-dependent accounting mappings | account mapping runtime | Journal fields of the reference left for their slices: mail alias, invoice reference type and model, invoice report (invoices); payment method lines, bank account and statement source (payments and bank statements); hash mode (locking); self-billing and the sequence override regex (numbering follow-up); dashboard computes (dashboard). account.account is ordered by id until the ordering slice adds the code order of SPEC-ACCLED-038, so a list cannot be sorted by the code yet. A condition on code (=, !=, in, not in, like, ilike, =like, =ilike and their negations, = False) matches the code of the active company's tree, as reading the code does: a branch searches its root's codes, and an account shared by two trees is found by the code of each tree in that tree. A negative operator also matches accounts without a code in the tree. Without an active company the condition is a Validation error. A name search (a many2one field) matches the name or the code as contained text; the reference matches the code by prefix. Internal users read account.code.mapping, so such a search works for anyone who may read accounts.

tax_ids holds default taxes and enforces the account's company applicability. A tax distribution's account_id restricts account deletion, including hidden/archived owners. The model-level refusal checks unlink authority first and gives no unreadable account labels. Archiving is supported; there is no deprecated field. See [Tax definitions](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/account-taxes.md#default-tax-links) for company/product defaults.

docs.title: Journal entries and journal items: drafts and posting

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

erp_addon_account::moves holds the journal entry header account.move ([AccountMove]) and its items account.move.line ([AccountMoveLine]). An entry is created, edited, checked for balance and deleted as a draft, then posted, cancelled or returned to draft through the posting service. Screens (form, list, search) come with the accounting UI tasks; the three operations are RPC methods for now.

| Model | Stored | Read through the entry or company | |---|---|---| | account.move | name, ref, date, state, move_type, journal_id, company_id, currency_id, partner_id | company_currency_id | | account.move.line | move_id, company_id, journal_id, date, parent_state (stored related of the entry), account_id, partner_id, name, sequence, display_type, currency_id, amount_currency, balance, is_storno, date_maturity | move_name, ref, company_currency_id | debit and credit are virtual generated columns over balance and is_storno (ADR 0048 D1); a storno line keeps a negative amount on its own side. Both models declare owner_only_stored_fields = []: another addon that adds a stored field to them fails the registry build (ADR 0048 D7) and keeps its data in a companion table instead. Default order: entries by date, then number, then id, all descending; items by date descending, then entry descending, then id (no copy of the entry number on the line).

- **Journal**: the first general journal (journal order) of the entry's company or one of its parents that the caller can read; one in the entry's currency first when a currency is given. None: a UserError asking for a journal. - **Company**: the active company when the journal belongs to it or to one of its parents, else the journal's company. - **Currency**: the journal's, else the company's. A line takes the entry's currency. - **Date**: today in the caller's time zone. **Type**: entry (invoice types arrive with the invoicing tasks). - Changing the journal of a draft clears its number (name), unless the same write gives one.

debit and credit are flagged input_adapted = true, so a create or write that names them reaches the line's _adapt_generated_input before the generated-column guard (ADR 0215), on every path (typed and dynamic calls, nested line_ids commands, imports): - debit = d gives balance = d, credit = c gives balance = -c, both together give d - c. - On a write, a side written as zero keeps the stored amount of the other side; a non-zero side replaces it. - Both sides non-zero on one line, or a balance that contradicts the debit and credit given with it, is refused (Validation). In the company currency amount_currency equals balance: the written one sets the other, and two different values are refused. Monetary values are rounded on their currency's increment by the ORM (ADR 0087).

When a line's currency is not the company currency, the amount that is not given is converted through the exchange rate (SPEC-ACCMOVE-014, 025, 032, 034): | Call | Given | Result | |---|---|---| | create | amount_currency only | balance = amount_currency converted into the company currency | | create | balance (or debit/credit) only | amount_currency = the balance converted into the line currency | | create | both, or neither | kept as given (zero when neither); no rate is read and the two are not compared | | write | amount_currency without balance | balance re-derived; with currency_id in the same write, in the new currency | | write | balance without amount_currency | the stored amount_currency is kept | | write | currency_id alone | both amounts are kept | - The rate is the spot rate of the entry's company (its root company's rates, else shared ones) on the entry's date, under the base rule RateDateRule::StrictlyBefore: the latest rate strictly before that date; with none before it, the earliest later one (erp_addon_base::money, SPEC-BASE-061). Invoices, which convert at their invoice date, are not delivered yet. - The rate is an exact ratio: no float is involved. The quotient is rounded once, on the increment of the currency it is converted into, half away from zero (CURRENCY_ROUNDING_MODE, ADR 0046 D2/D3). - A currency without any rate is refused with base's UserError, which names the currency, the company and the date. No rate of one is assumed. - Conversions are batched: one rate read per company and entry date (and per 255 currencies), never one per line. - The rates are read as the caller: internal users read res.currency.rate, so no right is added and nothing is elevated. - Rounding each line on its own can leave an entry that balances in the line currency unbalanced in the company currency (1, 1 and -2 EUR at a rate of 3 give 0.33, 0.33 and -0.67 USD). The balance check then refuses it like any other unbalanced entry. - A change of the entry date re-derives nothing on the server. In the reference this is form behaviour (onchange), not delivered yet.

After a create, write or delete of entries or lines, the touched entries must balance: one SQL aggregate over their lines, compared with zero exactly (amounts are on the currency increment). An unbalanced entry is a UserError that names the entry and the difference. Nested line_ids commands are checked once, after all of them ran. The context key check_move_validity = false skips the check (a form saving an incomplete draft); any value other than a boolean is a Programming error.

- An accountable line (display_type = product) needs an account; a section, subsection or note line has no amount and no account (named CHECK constraints). - move_id never changes: a write that moves a line to another entry, directly or through line_ids link commands, is refused. Delete the line and add a new one to the other entry. - Account, journal and partner must suit the entry's company (check_company). - Deleting an entry deletes its lines. - is_storno = true is refused until the company's storno setting exists (not delivered yet).

The state of an entry changes only through three methods of account.move (module moves::post); a caller-written state (or parent_state on a line) is refused, also as superuser. Each needs account.group_account_user (or superuser mode) and write access to every entry, and is atomic: a refusal leaves every entry as it was. - action_post ([post_moves]) posts draft entries. It collects every refusal of the batch and raises them together as one UserError, one line each: an entry not in draft, an entry without an accountable line, an archived journal, an inactive currency, an archived account, an account none of whose companies is the entry's company or one of its parents, an unbalanced entry. An entry dated where a lock date refuses it is re-dated to the day after the latest violated lock, adjusted to the journal's numbering reset (ADR 0147 D4, the reference's rule); the new date is checked again and a period that is not open refuses it. A missing fiscal period is refused naming ensure_periods. Then one statement sets the entries and their items to posted with the final date, and the entries take the next numbers of their journals (numbering, ADR 0048 D2.3 step 7): a credit note in the refund chain of a journal that keeps one (R before the code), everything else in the document chain. For plain entries the number of statements does not depend on the batch size. - The lock check holds the rows of the checked companies and their parents shared until the transaction ends: a lock date committed after the posting transaction began fails the posting with a serialization error (40001) and the unit of work is retried under the new date, and a lock-date change waits for postings in flight. - A draft that carries a name is refused with the collected checks: a posted entry never returns to draft, so such a name was written by hand, and it could repeat a posted number or take one the chain gives out later. Clear the name to post the entry. - The draft invoices of the batch are first rebuilt from their product lines (invoice::sync_lines), so a price, quantity, discount or tax written on an invoice line directly is in the tax line, the receivable or payable line and the totals before the invoice checks read them. This part writes each changed line and header on its own. - A re-dated entry keeps its company-currency balances; they are not converted again at the new date. - button_draft ([reset_moves]) returns cancelled entries to draft. A posted entry is refused: every company's posting policy is reversal-only (ADR 0146) until the opt-in policy exists; a posted entry is corrected by a reversal (not available yet). - button_cancel ([cancel_moves]) cancels draft entries; a posted one is refused for the same reason. An entry with a line that carries taxes, or with a tax line, reaches the tax report: the tax lock date binds it at posting and re-dates it like the other locks. A posted or cancelled entry keeps everything but its reference (moves::post::POSTED_MOVE_WRITABLE), and its items everything but their label and due date (POSTED_LINE_WRITABLE, both lists from ADR 0048 D3 R1b). Any other field written on one, the invoice fields included (invoice and due dates, totals, payment state, invoice lines, quantity, price, discount, product, subtotals) and state, is refused with a UserError that names the fields. The check runs on the final values of the write, after the invoice date has set the accounting date. Items cannot be added to such an entry or deleted from it, and it cannot be deleted. Adding, changing or deleting an item takes its entry's header row in id order with a version update, the order posting locks headers in. An item change and a posting of the same entry therefore never both commit: whichever commits second fails with a serialization error (40001), and its retry sees the other's result. These guards read and lock an entry by the id the caller gave, so they ask the caller's rights on that entry first: write access for a change of the entry or of its items (adding and deleting an item included), unlink access for a delete. A caller without them gets the access refusal, which never carries the state or the number of the entry, and takes no lock. Not delivered yet: the database guards on posted rows (the balance and line-state triggers of ADR 0048 D3 and the posting batch row), the markers that record a re-dating (ADR 0147 D4), the outbox event per posting batch, hashing, scheduled posting and invoice-specific checks. Upgrading account to 1.2 drops the draft-only CHECK constraints of the earlier version (migrations/1.2/pre-drop-draft-only-checks.sql).

account.group_account_readonly reads entries and items; account.group_account_user creates, writes and deletes them. Each model has the generated company rule of its company_id (exact company). The reference's invoicing group is not delivered yet.

Checked by the ORM for now, by triggers once the posted-row guards are delivered (ADR 0048 D3): company of accounts and journals (R4c), the line's entry never changing (R1a), amount in currency equal to the balance in the company currency (R4d), amounts on the currency increment (R4e).

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

Code: erp_addon_account::payterm (models and loading), payterm::compute (pure arithmetic, unit tests in test_compute.rs), payterm::partner (defaults) and invoice::sync (use on invoices). | Model | Notes | |---|---| | account.payment.term | name, note, active, sequence, optional company_id (access by branch ancestry), display_on_invoice, line_ids | | account.payment.term.line | value (percent or fixed), value_amount, delay_type, nb_days, days_next_month, payment_id | | account.move | invoice_payment_term_id (restricts deletion of a used term) | | res.partner | company-dependent property_payment_term_id (customer) and property_supplier_payment_term_id (vendor); both are commercial fields |

A constraint on the term (names name and line_ids) runs on every create and write: percent lines between 0 and 100 and adding up to 100 once rounded to the digits of the Payment Terms decimal precision (shipped as 6, setting: Technical > Decimal Precision; without a row the code uses 6). A constraint on each line checks the day of the next month (a number from 0 to 31). Editing one line directly, without writing its term, does not re-run the sum check: the invoice sync checks the percent sum again before it uses the terms and refuses an invalid term.

compute::instalments(lines, date_ref, total, total_currency, sign, company_increment, currency_increment): a percent line takes its share of each total, quantized once to the currency increment; a fixed line takes its amount with sign in the document currency and the company amount through the ratio of the two totals; the last line takes the exact remainder in both currencies. A fixed line on a document whose company or document total is zero is refused (no ratio exists). Dates: compute::due_date.

sync_terms (invoice/sync.rs) writes one payment_term line per instalment, matched to existing lines in id order (updated, added or deleted), and the header invoice_date_due is the latest instalment date. Without terms, or without an invoice or accounting date, one line is written as before. A new invoice takes the partner's terms of its kind and company unless the values or the context (default_invoice_payment_term_id) give one; writing partner_id on drafts of one kind and company does the same. Not yet: early payment discount, cash rounding, the instalment preview.

erp_addon_account::payment holds the payment account.payment ([AccountPayment]), the payment method account.payment.method and the method line account.payment.method.line (a method on one journal).

The addon ships two methods, Manual Payment inbound and outbound (data/account_payment_data.xml). Every bank, cash and credit-card journal created through the ORM, or changed into one, gets one line of each; journals that existed before version 1.3 of the addon get them at the 1.4 upgrade step, and the demo bank and cash journals their demo outstanding accounts there as on a fresh install (the step fails by name when the two methods did not load). A line's payment_account_id is the outstanding receipts (inbound) or payments (outbound) account of its payments. Methods and lines are written by accounting managers.

| Status | How it gets there | Journal entry | |---|---|---| | Draft | created | none (ADR 0048, parity treatment A4 W10) | | Paid | action_post | created and posted through moves::post_moves, numbered in the journal's payment chain (P before the code) | | Reconciled | its liquidity item is settled, or it is matched with invoices (or bills) that are all paid and its outstanding account is not a bank or cash account; or action_validate | unchanged | | Cancelled | action_cancel on a draft | none | state, name, move_id, the reconciliation flags, the outstanding account and is_sent are written by these actions only: a value given to create or write, or a default_* context key, is refused by name (a new payment may say state = "draft"). action_post never books a payment that already has an entry. The reference resets a confirmed payment and its entry to draft; under the reversal-only policy (ADR 0146) that is refused here. action_draft returns a cancelled or rejected payment to draft. A confirmed payment cannot be cancelled, reset or deleted, and its date, amount, partner, journal, method and accounts cannot change: its posted entry is undone by a reversal (ADR 0146), which is not built yet. The memo stays writable and becomes the entry's reference.

Posting builds one entry per payment: a liquidity item on the outstanding account (the method line's, else the root company's transfer account, else the payment is refused by name) and a counterpart item on the destination account (the one given, else the company's receivable or payable account, chosen as for invoices). Both carry the commercial partner, the payment date as due date and the label "method: memo". The entry's origin_payment_id links it to the payment and is written by the service only.

state, is_reconciled and is_matched are written by payment::refresh_payments, which runs in the unit that posts, matches or unmatches (reconcile::apply::refresh_moves, after the invoices' status). is_matched is also true when the outstanding account is the journal's own account. Callers cannot write them, nor name, move_id, outstanding_account_id and is_sent, given or as default_<field> context keys.

account.move.action_register_payment() (the Register Payment button of a confirmed invoice, bill or credit note) returns a dialog action on account.payment.register with default_invoice_ids. The transient model computes from its documents the company, the commercial partner, the direction (from the sign of the netted amount due), the amount due, the amount and the memo (the document numbers, sorted); the journal is the company's first bank journal, else its first cash journal, and the method line the journal's first line of the direction. journal_id and payment_method_line_id stay editable; amount and communication only while single_payment (the dialog makes one payment). A row is its creator's only (the access row's create_uid predicate, as the base wizards have) and of its documents' company. The client opens the dialog as a new record: its first onchange sees the documents as in-memory records, so the computes read their stored rows through the records' origin. The client then creates the dialog with one save that carries the documents and what the user entered (amount, memo, journal, method line). The company and its currency come from a read-only #[compute(candidate, ...)]: that only keeps such a create from being refused for an async currency. The documents are linked after the INSERT, so the company and currency arrive with the recompute that follows the link, and that recompute keeps what the row already holds: the entered amount and memo on the first computation, the chosen journal, and the chosen method line while it is a line of that journal and direction. action_create_payments() asks the write right on the dialog row and locks it, reads the documents after the caller's read check, refuses by name what cannot be paid together (not an invoice, bill or credit note; not confirmed; blocked; nothing left to pay; another currency than the company's; an amount due on several receivable or payable accounts; several companies; customer and vendor documents mixed; documents that cancel each other out; an amount of zero or less; an amount due that changed since the dialog opened; a changed amount when several payments would be made; a journal of neither the documents' company nor one of its parents; a payment method of the other direction), then creates the payments in the documents' company, each with the chosen method line, through account.payment.create with the caller's rights, posts them with post_payments and matches each payment's counterpart item with the documents' open items through reconcile_lines. With group_payment (the default) there is one payment per commercial partner and account; without it, one payment per document for its own amount due. When there is one payment it carries the entered amount. The dialog row is deleted with the registration, so a second call finds it gone (Missing) and registers nothing. The dialog closes with a notification naming the payments.

Read-only accounting users read payments; accounting users create, post, cancel and reset them (the posting and reconciliation services ask account.group_account_user); records are isolated per company.

Payments in another currency are posted (the items are converted at the payment date) but cannot be matched yet; duplicate detection, the receipt report, check printing, online providers, withholding lines, internal transfers, reversal of a confirmed payment come with their slices. The Register Payment dialog does not yet pay documents in other currencies, write off a difference, split installments, apply early-payment discounts or propose the partner's preferred method line.

erp_addon_account::reconcile matches the debit and credit items of one account with each other (ADR 0048 D4 with amendment A7, ADR 0050 D4/D5). This release covers posted items in the company currency on accounts that allow reconciliation (account.account.reconcile, always on for receivable and payable accounts).

| Model | What it holds | Written by | |---|---|---| | account.partial.reconcile | One match: debit item, credit item, amount (company currency and each item's currency), later date of the two, settlement | the service only; unlink unmatches | | account.full.reconcile | The settlement of a component whose items are all settled; its id is their matching number | the service only; unlink alone is refused | | account.open.item | What is still due on a matched item and its component label | the service only; users read it | Database CHECKs keep a match positive and between two different items, and an open item's residual between zero and the item's amount on the item's side, so an over-applied match fails whatever path writes it.

full_reconcile_id, matched_debit_ids and matched_credit_ids are written by the service only: a caller value or a default_<field> context key is refused by name. amount_residual, amount_residual_currency, reconciled and matching_number are computed in one read per batch: from the open-item row when the item belongs to a component that is not settled, zero when it is settled, else the item's own amounts. The number is the settlement id, else P with the smallest match id of the component, else empty. These four fields are not searchable yet.

- account.move.line.reconcile() takes the items in the order due date (else date), amount in currency, balance, grouped by partner when several take part, and matches debits with credits for the smaller open amount at each step. A settled item whose component has an open item in the selection is left out; any other settled item is refused, naming the entries it is matched with that the caller may read and counting the others. An item without an amount is refused as having nothing to match. - A matched journal item cannot be deleted, not even by SQL: the matches refer to their items with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, and so does an item's open-item row. - account.move.line.remove_move_reconcile() and unlink of a match remove matches; the residuals of the component are rebuilt from the matches that remain and the settlement goes. - unlink of a settlement on its own is refused (the reference keeps the matches and shows P numbers again; that comes later). The posted invoices among the entries get their amount due (what remains on their receivable or payable items) and their payment status (not paid, partial, paid, reversed) in the same unit, from one function (reconcile::apply::refresh_moves). The "in payment" status resolves to paid (plan decision L14). A changed status is reported to the record history (Transaction::track_external), so the invoice thread shows it when the accounting mail bridge is installed.

The caller needs account.group_account_user and write access to the items (read access to the matches when it deletes them); the check runs before any statement reads or locks a caller-named record. One unit takes, in order: the entry headers of every item reached through the matches (id order, with a version touch), their open items (line-id order), then the matches and settlements (id order). A second unit racing for the same items fails with a serialization error and applies nothing. One interactive call may reach at most 2,000 items and 4,000 matches.

Items of draft or cancelled entries; items in another currency than the company's; write-offs, cash-basis taxes, exchange differences and early-payment discounts. Open-item rows are created at an item's first match (the line triggers of ADR 0048 D4 are not built), so open-item lookups by account and partner do not cover unmatched items yet.

The account addon owns tax groups, tax definitions and invoice/refund repartition lines. This foundation configures definitions; the shared calculation kernel, fiscal positions, cash basis and journal-item usage probes are delivered by their respective slices. A tax belongs to one company and carries that company's root identity. Active taxes with a use other than none have a unique source-language name within the root company, use, scope and country. The database index protects concurrent writers; a normal create or write checks candidates in a batch to return a detailed conflict message. Translations do not create independent uniqueness namespaces. Change translated names through normal model writes in the desired language. Low-level native translation-map editing is a framework API, rather than a tax RPC; it relies on the database key instead of the model writer's detailed duplicate diagnostics. Tax amount and repartition percentages use exact decimal values. Send decimal strings through the normal RPC value conversion. Amount uses four decimal places and factor percent uses twelve. A tax's factor ratio is its percentage divided by 100, with exact decimal arithmetic. Creating a tax without distributions generates one base and one tax row for each document kind. Supply both invoice and refund changes in one parent operation: each side needs exactly one base row, at least one tax row, matching ordered types and percentages, and the required positive/negative totals. Direct child operations must leave the owning definitions valid too. A repartition row always has an owning tax, and its company follows that owner. The declared database setting account.tax_repartition_lines_max defaults to 16 lines per tax and document kind, including the base row. Its floor is 2 and hard bound 64. Accounting administrators change it in the Taxes settings block; invalid values are refused. Company fiscal country and the price-inclusion default are fields on the company. The address-country fallback follows company.partner_id.country_id, because the current base model stores the address country on its company contact. A tax may override price inclusion. No standalone taxes or groups are installed: chart/localization packs supply jurisdiction-specific definitions. Create a matching tax group before a tax when no chart has been loaded. Reference data is described in odoo/addons/account/data/template/account.tax-generic_coa.csv and account.tax.group-generic_coa.csv; these reference records are not copied into the addon. The used probe is an overridable model method. A referencing addon must extend it before introducing a relation that makes a tax used. The delete guard calls it and advises archiving a used definition. The foundation has no move or reconciliation references, so real usage detection remains incomplete until the journal-item and reconciliation integrations extend it. The audit trail records call identity, actor and targets through the existing core. Durable old/new repartition history belongs to the tax change-history integration and the core value-carrying change record. The current registry cannot track translated fields; translated tax-name capture is deferred explicitly. Do not claim tax change history from the foundation alone.

Install or upgrade account through the normal module lifecycle and verified addon identity receipts. Schema sync creates the new tables and source-name index; existing companies receive the excluded-price default. This does not load a chart. Configure the company's fiscal country, create an appropriate tax group, then create taxes. A missing country or group is refused rather than replaced by invented jurisdiction data. Existing account/journal records remain in place. This foundation requires no accounting-private history migration. If schema sync finds duplicate active source keys in a later imported database, repair the definitions explicitly before retrying; do not disable the index or silently rename records. A serialization failure during concurrent distribution edits is handled by the existing transaction retry boundary.

Extend _is_used as a batch method returning one boolean for each input record, in order, and retain the previous implementation. Unlink probes it afresh. Do not trust a cached display flag when enforcing deletion. New reference-bearing addons must add their probes before making a tax used. root_company_id, repartition_serial and a line's company_id are derived. Callers may not supply them. root_company_id is a stored computed field on company_id: a change of the tax's company, also one made by server code past the tax's own write, moves the root with it. Such a change keeps the tax's country and tax group as they are; write them in the same call when they must change too. Supply the owning tax_id on a direct line creation. Parent edits coordinate nested line mutations and validate the completed invoice/refund pair once; direct child edits validate their affected parents too. Every operation retains normal model, field and company admission. The plain tax form exposes the two distributions through the existing relation widget. Each grid passes its document side (default_document_type) to new lines, and the line views hide the document side and the owning tax. Complete side-by-side inline editing is outside this foundation. Configure custom splits atomically through a parent write until that editor is delivered.

The accounting addon extends companies with nullable account_sale_tax_id and account_purchase_tax_id. The company form's Taxes page edits them independently. These ordinary tax FKs enforce company consistency; the empty choice means no configured default. It does not mean that a document is tax exempt. The dedicated company-accounting form has a later stored view priority, so its explicit action leaves the general company form and its tax extensions available through ordinary company navigation. account.account.tax_ids provides account-level choices. Off-balance accounts cannot have default taxes, including when changing type and tax links together. A repartition-line reference prevents deleting its account; archiving remains supported. There is no legacy deprecated field. Accounting extends product.template with taxes_id and supplier_taxes_id; variants delegate to the template. For each direction, defaults collect the selected companies' choices. Only an empty collection falls back to inherited company defaults. Explicit choices, including explicit empty commands and contextual defaults, take precedence. The company-set product's choices must apply to that company or its ancestors. Shared-product choices may span selected companies and their ancestors; new targets retain caller read admission. Existing unreadable links survive replacement and clearing through the ORM's relation writer and are not returned by write. After every create, and after every write that supplies a tax field or the company, the stored links of a company-set product are checked again in the database, archived and unreadable taxes included; a tax of another company is refused without naming it. The stored readonly effective_account_sale_tax_id and effective_account_purchase_tax_id fields hold the configured company choice, else its parent's effective choice. Declared dependencies update inheriting descendants after an ancestor default changes. These fields are not Settings inputs; assigning them is refused. Product defaults read only selected company rows and omit unreadable tax targets. No explicit elevation or core API extension is used. Upgrading accounting creates the nullable company columns and tax relations without filling existing products or creating jurisdiction taxes. A later default change affects the next proposed product choice; it does not rewrite stored choices. No additional schedule, numeric limit or background job is introduced.

A product shared between companies receives editable defaults from the companies selected at creation only, with inherited defaults (a later release adds the rest). Defaults of unselected companies are not copied. The per-company resolver, explicit no-tax marker, inherited-choice display and document integration are not available yet. Do not infer tax exemption from an absent product link in another company.

The accounting application is two addons (ADR 0187). Both are exact_only = true: every money, quantity and rate column they add is an exact numeric column. | Addon | Depends on | Owns | |---|---|---| | analytic | base | analytic plans, analytic accounts, applicability, analytic lines and their members | | account | base, product, analytic | every table that references a journal item (including the distribution source tables of ADR 0142 and the mapping relations of ADR 0141), and everything else of the accounting application; it is an application | A later addon (project, timesheet, budgets) that needs analytic accounts depends on analytic only, not on the whole accounting application. Tables are created by the slice that needs them; the first one is the number chain table of account ([Journal entry numbering](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/accounting-numbering.md)). Dependencies the reference product lists and ERPForAll does not have yet (mail, portal, onboarding, digest) are added to the depends list by the slice that first uses them; the upgrade installs them. There is no base_setup addon (the settings page is part of base). The tax kernel is a library crate, not an addon. No other accounting sibling addon exists until a slice puts its first model in it, and the addons ship no install hook until a slice has install-time work.

The data list of addons/account/manifest.toml keeps this order: 1. security/account_security.xml (groups and record rules), first; 2. the default data of each model (data/*.xml); 3. views, wizard views and report actions; 4. menus, after the actions they point to; 5. security/ir.access.csv, last. There are no demo files until the onboarding slice. addons/account/tests/manifest_order.rs reads the manifest and fails if the security XML is listed anywhere but first or the access CSV anywhere but last.

addons/account/src/lib.rs holds only the erp_sdk::addon! call and alphabetically sorted mod lines; each slice family gets its own directory, so parallel slices do not touch the same file. Add a Cargo dependency on erp-addon-product or erp-addon-analytic in the slice that first imports a type from it. Fiscal-position setup and native mapping methods: [Fiscal-position resolution](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/fiscal-positions.md).
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

Status: implemented. Design: ADR 0048 D3 R2 (period records), ADR 0147 D2, D7 and D8 (one calendar with an accounting and a stock status, reopening, the two-step locks). Behaviour: docs/specs/accounting/locking.md (SPEC-ACCLOCK-023, -099 to -103). Code: addons/account/src/fiscal/. The reference keeps lock dates on the company and compares every date with them. ERPForAll keeps those company dates for display and for their setters, and stores one account.fiscal.period row per company and month: the row's statuses are what writers decide on, because only a row can be locked and drained safely (ADR 0147 D8). The stock addon never reads this table; stock asks through stock_account (ADR 0147 G5).

| Column | Meaning | |---|---| | company_id, fiscal_year, kind, number | unique together; fiscal_year is the year of the fiscal year's last day; kind is regular (numbers 1 to 12) or adjustment (13 to 16, one day long, created by the year close) | | date_from, date_to | the range, both days included; regular periods of a company never overlap (an exclusion constraint) | | status | open, closed (fiscal-year lock), hard_locking, hard_locked; a CHECK refuses any other value, and period_admission returns an internal error naming the period for a value it does not know (never Open) | | stock_lock_status | open, stock_locking, stock_locked (a CHECK); a hard_locked period is always stock_locked (a CHECK) | | *_started_by, *_started_at | set exactly while the matching lock is in progress (a CHECK) | | stock_lock_generation, hard_lock_generation | run counters of the two locks | | closed_at, hard_locked_at | when the period left open, when it reached hard_locked | The record API refuses create, write and delete, also with elevated rights; the readonly accounting group reads the periods of its companies. No default rows ship: periods are created when something needs them. The company has fiscalyear_lock_date, tax_lock_date, sale_lock_date, purchase_lock_date, hard_lock_date, stock_lock_date, and the internal counter fiscal_period_serial. The three specialized soft dates default to unset. Hard and stock dates move through their owning lock operations, never a generic company write.

use erp_addon_account::fiscal::ensure_periods; // caller: the BeginOptions of the unit that needs the periods (its principal and context) let created: u64 = ensure_periods(&orm, caller, company_id, date_from, date_to).await?; It creates the missing regular periods containing a day of the range for the company's root and every branch, from the root's fiscal calendar, and returns the number of rows created. Call it **outside** the unit of work that needs the periods (before its first statement, or after it failed for a missing period and before it is restarted): it runs in its own short transactions as caller (the settings read, then the insert at READ COMMITTED), so the new rows are visible to the restarted unit. It is idempotent; two concurrent calls for the same month both succeed. Statuses of new rows are derived from the company lock dates, the latest over the company and its ancestors. A date beyond the horizon setting, a range needing more than 1,200 periods, or a fiscal year end that no longer matches the existing periods is refused by name. ensure_periods_with takes a calendar read once with FiscalCalendar::read (or built with FiscalCalendar::new, which checks the horizon bounds), for imports that ensure many ranges.

Company settings, block "Fiscal periods" of the Accounting settings page, read from the root company: | Key | Default | Bounds | |---|---|---| | account.fiscalyear_last_day | 31 | 1 to 31, and a day the month has (29 February accepted) | | account.fiscalyear_last_month | December | January to December | | account.fiscal_period_horizon_months | 12 | 1 to 120 | Periods are one month long (ADR 0048 D3 R2). A fiscal year ending on the 15th has periods from the 16th to the 15th; a February end of 28 or 29 means the month end. Changing the fiscal year end after periods exist makes the next ensure_periods that would overlap them fail loudly. The day and the month are checked together on every settings write (the setting group account.fiscal_year_end): setting February while the day stays 31 is refused, naming both keys. A branch shows the block too but its values are not used; it follows its root company. Hiding the block at branch scope needs a scope the settings framework does not have yet.

use erp_addon_account::fiscal::{WriteClass, period_admission, require_open_periods}; let verdicts = period_admission(tx, WriteClass::Accounting, &[(company_id, date)]).await?; let period_ids = require_open_periods(tx, WriteClass::Stock, &rows).await?; // refuses every lock One verdict per (company, date): Open, NoPeriod (run ensure_periods, restart), FiscalLock (an accounting writer applies its re-dating policy, planned with posting; a stock writer refuses), HardLock (everyone refuses), StockLock (stock class only). Accounting writers ignore the stock status. The call takes the shared advisory lock (PERIOD_LOCK_CLASS, period_id) of each period first, so a lock operation's T1 waits for in-flight writers and its drain covers the rest. Call it once per batch at the start of the writer's unit of work. Sale, purchase and tax soft locks, exceptions and the backdating window are not period-row questions; the lock and posting work adds them.

The status operations all require account.group_account_manager and take the exclusive advisory locks of the periods they may change, in id order. **Who may act on which company (SPEC-ACCLOCK-104).** Outside superuser mode every period operation, ensure_periods and period_admission act only on a company in the caller's active companies (Transaction::companies) or on a branch below one: a branch follows its parent's lock dates, as in the reference (odoo/addons/account/models/company.py:572-577). Anything else is refused with Access ("One of the selected companies does not exist or is not one of yours."), also for a period or company id that does not exist, so the answer does not tell whether it exists. Superuser mode is not limited. **What the synchronisation waits for (SPEC-ACCLOCK-105).** sync_lock_dates first takes the exclusive advisory lock of every period whose status it may change, before its refusal checks and its updates. A writer that was admitted for such a period (it holds the shared lock) commits first; a writer that asks after the synchronisation committed sees the new status. The wait is bounded by the transaction's lock_timeout (OrmConfig::timeouts, or BeginOptions::timeouts for the unit); the lock operations' own SET LOCAL lock_timeout is planned. A writer whose transaction already read the period before the synchronisation committed (a repeatable-read snapshot) still sees the old status: for the hard lock the drain of the two-step run covers it; for the fiscal-year lock nothing does yet, and the case is left to the lock-date setters (planned). A synchronisation that would change more than 1,200 periods per company of the tree at once is refused; move the lock date in smaller steps. **Same transaction, one lock order.** sync_lock_dates flushes the transaction first, so a setter may write the lock date through the record API and call it right after. Every path takes its locks in one order: the target company row, then the root company row (fiscal_period_serial), then the period advisory locks in id order; the second step of a lock run takes the two company rows FOR UPDATE first, so a setter and a lock run on the same company wait for each other instead of deadlocking. That second step needs a READ COMMITTED transaction (BeginOptions::isolation(Isolation::ReadCommitted)); in a REPEATABLE READ one it is refused with Programming. - sync_lock_dates(tx, company_id): after a setter wrote a company lock date, closes and reopens periods to match, and reopens the stock status when the stock lock date was lowered. Refused, before writing, when the fiscal-year lock would reopen a hard-locked or a stock-locked period, or when a hard or stock lock date was moved past the periods its operation locked. - PeriodSet::of(tx, period_id): the period and the matching periods of its company's branches. - hard_lock_begin / hard_lock_complete / hard_lock_reset and stock_lock_begin / stock_lock_complete / stock_lock_reset: T1 (returns a LockRun with the generations), the T2 write when the counts are zero (writes the company date with GREATEST and bumps the root's serial), and the T2 refusal or audited cancel. Both locks run in order: T1 is refused while an earlier regular period of the company has not reached that lock. A T2 that matches no row returns LockOutcome::NotApplied with the period states (cancelled, superseded, or already locked by the hard lock). The caller owns the rest of each operation: SET LOCAL lock_timeout, committing T1, the drain, the counts T2 checks (drafts, unreconciled statement lines, readiness, replay jobs), and the close_period precondition for companies on the valuation bridge (ADR 0147 G4). Those are planned. Not yet: tax_return_id and the tax-return close, the adjustment periods' creation, the database trigger that refuses writes to locked rows from raw SQL (it needs addon-declared SQL objects), and the stuck display of an interrupted lock.

The native erp_addon_account::locking API provides `LockCheck::new(company, date, JournalClass, TaxImpact) and check_lock_dates(tx, &checks)`. Construct inputs from authorized business records. The result preserves input order: LockVerdict::Allowed or a typed refusal. into_result() retains its precise error kind and message. Fiscal-year and hard dates bind every accounting journal; sales and purchase dates bind their journal classes only; tax dates bind report-affecting changes only. A cutoff is inclusive. Effective dates take the maximum over the company and its ancestors. A branch's own date never restricts its parent. Hard-locking period rows bind checks before the company hard date advances. A period that is merely missing does not refuse a post: action_post creates the periods its entries need inside its own unit of work before the lock check (fiscal::ensure::ensure_for_rows, which checks the companies against the environment the post was authorised with). It creates only the periods that contain a posted date, for the root company and its tree, not the months between two dates. Two units that create the same new month at the same time: the second waits for the first one's commit and then fails with a serialization failure. Inside a retried unit of work (Orm::run, as the RPC layer runs every call) the retry finds the period and posts; a caller that runs the unit itself without a retry sees that failure and posts again. A date beyond the horizon setting, a lock date and a closed or locked period still refuse. Other writers that ask period_admission directly still get NoPeriod for a missing period. Call once per batch in the same transaction that writes the records. State is private to the call; subsequent calls reread it, including after savepoint rollback. There is no process cache or reusable permission token. Entry and line hooks are still being integrated, so calling this function is not proof that every entry mutation already enforces it. Transaction-wide caching and user exceptions are not implemented. change_lock_dates(tx, company, &LockPatch::new().set(LockField::Sale, Some(date))) changes soft dates. An omitted field is unchanged; None clears it. Accounting-manager rights and company scope are required. Generic company writes use the same policy and support one company per lock-date patch. Company creation accepts only unset dates. Future dates are refused using the caller environment's current-date helper, on every path that changes them (ADR 0206). A fiscal-year change calls sync_lock_dates and therefore respects hard/stock reopening refusals. Sale, purchase and tax changes do not close fiscal periods. Company dates, period changes and the typed change record in the audit trail commit together; audit failure rolls everything back. A no-op records no change event. The operation uses a savepoint, so a caught refusal does not leave partial dates or audit events. Hard activation is explicitly unavailable until the maintenance drain, ledger/bank checks, activation audit and applicable valuation-close checks are proven. The status primitives above are low-level building blocks, not a safe user-facing activation coordinator. Draft/unreconciled-line checks, exceptions, automatic date shifting and the lock-date wizard remain incomplete. Existing repeatable-read writers retain their snapshots; this foundation adds no soft-lock drain. The multi-company foundation verifies the native policy across root, branch, grandchild and sibling companies. A branch uses the maximum applicable cutoff from its ancestor chain; its own later cutoff does not restrict its parent or sibling. Diagnostics retain all applicable cutoffs in date order. These are native-policy guarantees only: the ACCMC tests remain partial until the entry owners integrate posting, reset and editing paths. User lock exceptions remain unimplemented under ADR 0206.
