Use erp_addon_account::mapping::CompanyDefault in a caller-owned transaction. A key identifies one company and a DefaultRole. Chart packs can parse the stable role keys receivable, payable, income, expense and stock_valuation with DefaultRole::from_key. Resolve each pack's account identifier to an account.account record in that company before calling install_if_absent. A return value of false means the company already has that default, which may be explicitly empty. Propagate errors from setup so they roll back the chart activation. At the chart activation boundary, erp_cli::module::chart_defaults::ChartAccountDefaults::prepare maps company defaults from a staged res.company record to installed account IDs. Pass the identity map of the selected template using each account reference's canonical pack key. The five mapping fields are receivable_account_id, payable_account_id, income_account_id, expense_account_id and account_stock_valuation_id. Omitted fields leave the company alone. Explicit template clears prepare empty choices, and unresolved references fail before writing any role. apply uses the activation transaction and rolls back every choice on refusal. The surrounding activation workflow owns authorization to activate a release and any approved replacement of settings an administrator edited. set records an ordinary change. A user needs company write and accounting-manager permission. The target must be readable, active, applicable to the company and valid for the role. The receivable and payable roles require their exact ledger account types. Income and expense follow the shared posting-account domain. The stock valuation role accepts current, non-current, fixed and prepayment asset types. A branch can use an eligible ancestor's account through its own key. resolve returns the account or an empty choice. require raises a configuration error when the role has no account. Both accept ResolutionDate::Current for the company's business date at transaction start and ResolutionDate::Document for a supplied business date. An invalid configured account produces an error. A role's first revision applies to earlier dates, and ordinary changes after that first revision apply from the transaction's local business date. An existing installation receives the four mapping tables and the role declarations through the normal native account upgrade with the matching release artifact. Role data uses stable external IDs, and account values come from the chart. Companies can have no mapping keys before a chart loads. Apply the standard runtime grant verification for the new tables before activation. The remaining sections describe the full ADR 0141 property design. The effective field adapter and search, account-merge lifecycle, posting evidence and sealed-horizon guards are follow-up work.

Account choices on a partner, product template or product category belong to one company. A proposed mapping records a typed subject, company, account role and account reference. A variant uses its template's account properties. Account roles include receivable/payable, income/expense and stock valuation where appropriate to the subject. Journals remain separately typed configuration. Ordinary fields read and search the effective property value: an explicit account or false value, otherwise the declared company default for that property. Writing the company-default value stores no independent override, so a later default change reaches that record. An explicit different account stays fixed. False against a nonempty default stays explicitly empty; restoring the default removes that override. Raw-override inspection is a separate internal operation. The property default is scoped to its subject kind: a category income default does not automatically fill the template field. The product business resolver can still obtain an account from its category. Global and per-user account defaults are excluded. Company receivable/payable defaults feed partner properties and invoice term selection. Existing move accounts retain priority; after the effective partner choices are exhausted, a missing configuration error replaces arbitrary active-account selection. Fiscal-position mapping follows selection.

The proposed resolver accepts bounded batches with explicit company, business date, required roles and the caller's transaction. It retains the configuration revision used. A missing required account is an error after permitted fallbacks are exhausted. An invalid configured account is an error immediately; it cannot silently become a default. Configuration changes append dated Account, Empty (explicit false), or Clear (inherit again) revisions. Company generations identify snapshots. Optional expected versions detect changes to the individual mapping key; unrelated edits in the same company do not cause a conflict. Ordinary writes without an expected version are accepted with last-writer-wins per key. Posted valuation contributions retain their selected account and category evidence; later edits do not reinterpret their reports. Transfers/corrections have explicit effects. Authorized account/partner merges append target mappings and lineage. Identical destination choices coalesce; conflicting choices require an explicit validated resolution. Source identities remain tombstones while old FK references exist. Segment payloads are not rewritten. Journal deletion is likewise restricted while retained configuration references it. Role policies define direct-category versus ancestor traversal, applicable costing modes, the property-default association and post-resolution hooks. Price difference uses only the direct category for standard cost, without a parent/company price-difference fallback. Close balancing uses direct category then closing-company valuation; stock posting uses its company journal. These callers must not be forced through one generic fallback chain.

Mapping rows obey company and subject access rules even for shared products or contacts. Account applicability checks remain separate from authorization and stay active under elevation. Shared category edits authorize companies whose accounting dependencies change, not every company with a shared product. Database guards cover mapping writes and account/journal applicability changes, including guarded SQL/import paths. See [company consistency](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/company-consistency.md) for the existing company context and integrity rules. Future addons consume declared account roles through the accounting addon API. Bridges supply stock integration. Chart installation, effective property wiring and rendered settings have their own acceptance checks.

docs.title: Journal entry numbering: number chains and the allocation point

sections.text: <!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0 -->

Status: implemented. Design: ADR 0048 D2 (numbering point and lock order). Behaviour: docs/specs/accounting/numbering.md (ACCSEQ). The posting step that calls this service is not available yet; until then the tests number a stand-in document (crates/erp-test-models/src/test_numbering.rs).

account.sequence.chain holds one row per (journal_id, kind, period_key), unique in the database. The row's next_number is the number the next document of the chain gets; last_name is the last name it handed out. | Column | Meaning | |---|---| | kind | the sequence kind: document, refund or payment (a selection: another addon adds a kind with selection_add; the debit-note addon will add debit) | | period_key | the reset period of the journal's declared pattern: never, 2026, 2026-07, 2025-26 or 2025-26-07 (see [Sequences](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/sequences.md)) | | company_id | the journal's company; internal users of that company or a branch of it may read the row | Rows are created on first use. Only the numbering service writes them: users have read access only. There are no default records: the reference keeps no such table (its next number is read from the highest entry name).

use erp_addon_account::numbering::{assign_numbers, LockWait, NumberRequest}; let wait = LockWait::from_settings(tx).await?; let requests: Vec<NumberRequest<'_>> = moves.iter().map(|m| NumberRequest { document_id: m.id, company_id: m.company_id, journal_id: m.journal_id, kind: "document", pattern: &journal_pattern,     // the journal's declared SequencePattern for this kind date: m.date, fiscal_year: m.fiscal_year,    // the move company's fiscal year; needed by the fiscal resets reference: m.reference.as_deref(), }).collect(); let numbers = assign_numbers(tx, wait, &requests).await?; // write numbers[i].name, .sequence_number and .chain_id on the documents, in the same transaction assign_numbers: 1. groups the requests by chain and orders each chain's documents by (date, reference, id), a missing reference sorting as empty text and text compared by code point (the reference's posting order); 2. sets the configured wait as the transaction's lock_timeout; 3. creates the missing chain rows, then locks every chain row of the batch with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, in (journal_id, kind, period_key) order (lock step 4 of ADR 0048 D2.1); 4. raises each chain's counter with one UPDATE and renders the names with the pattern; 5. puts the transaction's own lock_timeout back and returns the numbers in request order. Call it **last** in the posting transaction: the chain rows stay locked until that transaction commits or rolls back, so only the numbering step and the commit run under the lock. The document table must carry the two unique rules of ADR 0048 D2.5, UNIQUE (journal_id, name) and UNIQUE (chain_id, sequence_number): then the database itself refuses a duplicate number, whatever path wrote it.

| Situation | What happens | |---|---| | Two postings take numbers of the same chain | the second waits for the first. When the first commits, the second fails with Concurrency/40001 (a REPEATABLE READ transaction may not see the new counter); Orm::run runs its unit again and it takes the next number. Keep posting inside Orm::run. | | A posting rolls back, or a savepoint around the numbering rolls back | the counter rolls back with it: the next posting gets the same number, so no gap appears | | The chain is held longer than the configured wait | the call fails with Lock, SQLSTATE 55P03 and Condition::LockTimeout, naming the chain and the setting. It is never retried, by this service or by Orm::run. | | A transaction that has not reached the numbering step | holds no chain lock and blocks no other posting | | One batch asks for a chain with two patterns or two companies, an undeclared kind, a document twice, or a fiscal pattern without a fiscal year | Validation (or Programming for the missing fiscal year), before any statement |

| Setting | Scope | Default | Floor | Hard bound | |---|---|---|---|---| | account.sequence_lock_wait_ms | database (Settings page, block "Journal entry numbering") | 5,000 ms | 100 ms | 60,000 ms | LockWait::from_settings reads it with the framework's rights (the poster needs no settings group); LockWait::from_millis builds a wait inside the same bounds and refuses any other value by name.

- the journal's declared pattern fields and the journal_id many2one; - writing the numbers on account.move in the posting step, hand-typed and imported names; - the resequence engine, derived gap flags and the chain-end deletion rule, the opt-in gap-allowed mode, and the self-billing partner kind: planned as follow-up work.

The account addon owns fiscal positions and their account mappings. Taxes carry fiscal_position_ids and original_tax_ids; replacing_tax_ids reads the inverse of the same replacement relation. There is no separate position-tax model. A position's company, sequence, automatic-selection flag, VAT requirement, country/group/states and ZIP bounds are record configuration. Sequence starts at zero and uses the signed integer field's bounds. An unset criterion does not restrict matching. Archive a position to remove it from automatic selection.
Use ordinary model dispatch in an environment whose active company is the document's company:

let positions = tx.env().with_company(company)?.records("account.fiscal.position")?; let selected: Option<i64> = positions.call(tx, "_get_fiscal_position", (partner, None::<i64>)).await?; let rule = positions.browse(selected)?; let mapped: Vec<i64> = rule.call(tx, "map_tax", (taxes,)).await?;

_get_fiscal_position(partner_id, delivery_id) returns an optional id. Manual positions on the selected delivery address take precedence over the invoice partner's manual position; a manual position wins before automatic predicates. The EU-prefix/address exception can select the invoice address instead. Without a manual rule, an invoice partner lacking a country yields no rule. Candidates come from the selected company's ancestor chain and sort by company depth, sequence and id. _fpos_matches(partner_id) is a singleton predicate. An addon overrides it through Super dispatch, retaining the previous result and conjoining its own condition. Partners expose _get_vat_required_valid() for a similar extension. Both are internal native methods; declaring an override does not expose a new RPC method. map_tax(Vec<i64>) returns ordered, deduplicated destination ids. A global tax or a tax linked to this position can map to itself; a tax linked exclusively elsewhere is removed. Active replacements can be one-to-many. An empty position retains the input. map_account(i64) returns a mapped account id or its original id. Read access is checked on inputs, the position and outputs. The client tax picker (web_name_search) applies dynamic_fiscal_position_id before ordering and limiting. It accepts false or a positive position id, preserves the caller's own domain and access rules, and includes unassigned taxes. The generic native Records::name_search helper does not pass through this web-specific override.

Tax/account maps are derived from their relations. Company domestic selection prefers the lowest sequence and, on a tie, an explicit country over a group. The company's address country comes from its representative partner. This differs from foreign-VAT validation, which uses the configured fiscal country. Partner manual positions are company-dependent and use the existing commercial-field propagation mechanism. Install or upgrade account through the normal module lifecycle. Version 1.1 adds the position/mapping tables, tax relations and company/partner/group fields. Existing companies receive an internal zero revision for concurrency fencing. This field is unavailable through field access and is never a configuration control; a company create or write that supplies it is refused, in superuser mode too (data files, imports and sudo callers included). Concurrent writers with a stale snapshot can receive a serialization error; the existing whole-unit transaction boundary controls retries. Default country groups and their fiscal exception states are installed as editable, non-overwritten data. No universal company position or account mapping is installed; company-specific chart packs supply those defaults later. Internal users can read rules; accounting administrators can create, edit and delete them. Company and relation checks remain active under the normal ORM paths.

National validation of foreign VAT identifiers is unavailable. Saving a string trims it, removes spaces, dots and hyphens, uppercases it and refuses a string that becomes empty. This normalization does not establish legal validity. Explicit null clears the optional identifier. Equal normalized foreign identifiers can be used by several positions; a different identifier in the checked ancestor scope is refused. A refusal names the existing position only when the caller can read it. The dedicated configuration screens, document-line application, price adaptation, chart-driven foreign-tax creation, provider integration and optional date windows are separate deliveries. No process-global matching cache or measured speed claim is made.

A localization pack is data for one or more countries (a chart of accounts, taxes, dated rates) shipped inside an ordinary addon directory (ADR 0047). It has no code. The addon's manifest.toml stays the only place for dependencies, the package version and requested capabilities; pack.toml describes the data. A runnable example, also used by the tests, is crates/erp-modules/tests/fixtures/pack_sample/. Staging (erp_modules::pack::PackRegistry::stage_dir) reads local files only, checks the whole pack, and registers the release or refuses the first problem. A refusal names the file, the position inside it and the rule, for example data/accounts.csv: row 2.mystery: [unknown-field] Unknown pack field mystery.. Staging does not activate a chart for a company; that is a separate step.

| Key | Rule | |---|---| | format_version | 1. Another value is refused naming the version found and the supported set. | | pack_id, profile_id | Lower-case dotted names; the profile id starts with the pack id. | | rule_release_id | Immutable id of this release, 1 to 64 characters. The same id with other bytes is refused. | | pack_version | The pack's own version, a positive integer. A new release of the pack must be greater. | | release_date | YYYY-MM-DD. A new release may not be dated earlier than the previous one. | | jurisdictions | ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes. | | [schemas] | Model name to the SHA-256 of the offline schema the pack was written against. A model the pack uses must be listed; a wrong hash is refused. Nothing is fetched from a URL. | | [[files]] | path, sha256 of the bytes, kind (records or translations), model (the model of a record file: required for CSV, the default for TOML records). Every declared file must exist and match its digest. | | [dependencies."other.pack"] | release and sha256 of a staged release of another pack (see "Packs that build on other packs"). | | [[template]] | key, optional country (an ISO 3166 alpha-2 code that is one of the pack's jurisdictions; any other value is refused as jurisdiction at template[i].country), optional parent and code_digits (see "Child templates"), and files. Every file belongs to exactly one template. | Paths are relative and stay inside the pack: .., absolute paths, backslashes, symbolic links, hard links and URLs are refused. A path has one spelling: an empty or . component (data//a.toml, data/./a.toml, a leading or trailing slash) is refused where the file is declared, so two spellings of one file cannot both pass the duplicate check. The profile_id is the pack_id or the pack_id, a dot and more (example.sample.generic, not example.samplex).

Records are TOML tables. A record is identified by the pack, its template, its model and its key; names and codes are values, never identity. [[record]] model = "example.tax" key = "vat_std" [record.fields] name = "Standard rate" account = "sales"                  # a reference: key of a record of the schema's model rate = "decimal:10.0 percent"      # exact values carry a tag and a unit factor = "ratio:11/12 factor" - **Exact values** are decimal:<n> <unit> (at most 29 coefficient digits and scale 28, the ADR 0046 range) or ratio:<n>/<d> <unit> (positive denominator, at most 1232 digits). A TOML float or number, or a string without a tag, is refused. Stored decimals are canonical (-000.500 becomes -0.5). - **Dates** are 2026-01-01 (TOML dates or text). There is no "today": nothing reads the clock. - **References** are the key of a record of the schema's model in the same template. An unresolved reference is refused.

A records file ending in .csv is a flat table of one model (the model of its [[files]] entry). The first row names the columns: key, the fields of the model, and optionally template and tombstone (true, false or empty). Every row has as many cells as the header. key,name,code,note petty,Petty cash,15, card,Card,16,Card payments - A cell is typed by the schema field: text, integer, true or false, a date, an exact decimal: or ratio: value, or a reference (key, or other.pack/key). - An empty cell of a **new** record is an empty string for a text field and null for a nullable field of another type; an empty cell of a required field that is not text is refused ("Required pack field rate is empty."). The empty cells of a tombstone row are ignored. A TOML row that gives "" for a required text field is refused the same way ("Required pack field name is missing."). - An empty cell of a row that **overrides** an inherited record is refused ("Empty override cell note requires clear_fields or an explicit typed value."): omission inherits, so state a value, or clear the field in a TOML record with clear_fields. - A repeated or empty column name is refused. A column the model does not have is refused ("Unknown pack field"). Everything of the Odoo source CSV that carries meaning outside the cell is refused with one message, "Source CSV grammar is not accepted at runtime; use the offline localization converter.": a row with no key (a continuation row), a column name with a slash (account_id/id) or @lang, and a reference cell that is a comma list or a command tuple such as (6,0,[1]). Nested relations and translations are separate keyed rows.

A file of kind = "translations" is a CSV with exactly the columns model,key,field,lang,text: one row per record, text field and language. model,key,field,lang,text example.account,cash,name,fr,Caisse example.account,cash,name,pt_BR,Caixa The record must exist in the template (own or inherited), the field must be a text field of its model, lang is a language code (fr, pt_BR), text may not be empty, and a (model, key, field, lang) appears once. The label of a record is never a lookup key. A child template inherits the translations of its parent, can translate again (its own row replaces the inherited one), and loses the translations of a record it removes. They are read from TemplateData::translations. A translation file belongs to a template like any other file.

A pack names the releases of other packs it uses and pins each by digest: [dependencies."example.sample"] release = "R1" sha256 = "<digest of the staged release, Pack::digest>" [[template]] key = "local" parent = "example.sample/chart"        # a template of the pinned release files = ["data/local.toml"] - Parents and qualified references (example.sample/sales) resolve in the pinned release only; a newer release of the other pack is never substituted. A release that is not staged yet is refused ("Unresolved or undeclared pack reference ..."); a staged release with another digest is refused (digest-mismatch, path dependencies.example.sample). Stage the other pack first. - The child inherits the parent's effective records, translations and code_digits; the models of inherited records need not be declared again in [schemas]. Record::template keeps naming the template that defined a record. - A reference to a pack that is not a declared dependency is refused. A reference qualified with the pack's own id is a local one. - A pack never edits a template of another pack: a record row naming one is refused ("cannot extend template ... in place; declare a child template"). - The addon dependency that makes the other pack's addon load first is the manifest's, as always; this table pins the data release.

A template may name a parent: the key of another template of the same pack (or this.pack/key). Parents are resolved root first. The child starts from the parent's effective records and its own file rows override them by (model, key): a field the row names replaces the inherited value, a field it leaves out is inherited. A pack never edits a template it does not own: a row whose template names another template is refused with "cannot extend template ... in place; declare a child template".
[[template]] key = "chart_child" parent = "chart" files = ["data/child.toml"]

[[record]]                         # override: the name changes, the code is inherited model = "example.account" key = "bank" [record.fields] name = "Current account" [[record]]                         # clear: the nullable field becomes null (Value::Null) model = "example.account" key = "cash" clear_fields = ["note"] [[record]]                         # tombstone: the inherited record is removed from this template and its children model = "example.account" key = "misc" tombstone = true - **Clearing.** Omission inherits; clear_fields stores null and only a nullable field of an inherited record can be cleared. Clearing a field and giving it a value in the same row is refused, and so is clearing a non-nullable field. To override text with an empty string write the typed value note = ""; an empty string never means null. - **Tombstones.** A tombstone must name an inherited record and carries no fields. The removed keys are listed in TemplateData::tombstones for the activation step to evaluate; a record that still points at a removed record is refused as an unresolved reference. A later child may add the key again. - **Depth and cycles.** A parent chain longer than l10n.pack.max_parent_depth is refused ("Template parent depth exceeds configured limit."), and a loop is refused with the chain ("Template parent cycle: a -> b -> a."). - **Identity.** An effective record keeps its model and key; Record::template says which template defined or last overrode it. Child collections match by key, never by position. A parent in another pack is declared in [dependencies] (see "Packs that build on other packs").

code_digits on a template (a child inherits it, or sets its own) pads the code of every record whose model schema names a code_field, the way the reference charts do: zeros are added on the **right** (12 becomes 1200), so an account keeps its class. Only active accounts are padded: a record whose schema active_field is false keeps its code as written (such accounts are usually parents). A code longer than the width stays as it is: nothing is truncated and nothing is refused for length. Two codes that are equal after padding are refused ("Account code 1200 collides in root chart."); the record key, not the code, stays its identity, and nothing matches by prefix. code_digits = 0 is refused, and so is a width above l10n.pack.max_code_digits (before any padding). A template without code_digits keeps its codes as written. The name after root in the collision message is the root template of the parent chain, which owns one code space. A child that sets a wider code_digits pads the inherited codes again to the new width.

A model whose schema declares scope fields is dated: each row has valid_from and an optional exclusive valid_until. In one scope (for example jurisdiction and key) the ranges are non-empty and do not overlap. Nothing reads the clock. A changed rate is a new release that adds a row; the old release stays staged.

[origin] is required and checked at staging. | Key | Rule | |---|---| | kind | authored (written from primary sources). converted and mixed are refused in this release; see "Not in this format release". | | publisher, licence | Required. The licence is an SPDX expression of permissive terms only (the list in deny.toml, ADR 0157: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, Zlib, MPL-2.0 and the others there). A OR B needs one allowed term, A AND B all of them; GPL, LGPL and AGPL are refused, as is any unknown term. | | source_document, source_version, verified_on, reviewer, review_status | Required: the primary document and its version, the date it was read or verified, the reviewer, and pending or reviewed. | Data from Odoo Enterprise is never admitted. Indonesian packs are authored from primary sources.

Each cap is a system parameter with a default, a floor and a hard bound; a value outside them is refused naming the key, and zero never means unlimited. The loader receives them through PackLimits::from_params. | Key | Default | Floor | Hard bound | |---|---|---|---| | l10n.pack.max_total_bytes | 8 MiB | 1 KiB | 64 MiB | | l10n.pack.max_file_bytes | 2 MiB | 1 KiB | 16 MiB | | l10n.pack.max_files | 64 | 1 | 512 | | l10n.pack.max_rows | 100000 | 1 | 1000000 | | l10n.pack.max_fields_per_row | 64 | 1 | 256 | | l10n.pack.max_string_bytes | 4096 | 16 | 65536 | | l10n.pack.max_ref_edges | 200000 | 1 | 2000000 | | l10n.pack.max_parent_depth | 8 | 1 | 32 | | l10n.pack.max_code_digits | 16 | 1 | 256 | | l10n.pack.max_templates | 64 | 1 | 1024 | | l10n.pack.max_dependencies | 16 | 1 | 64 | l10n.pack.max_rows counts the rows of every records, translations and CSV file as they are read (a CSV file is refused as soon as the running count passes the limit) and also the records and translations a child template inherits from its parent: a parent with 1,000 records and 30 children counts 30,000 more. The refusal of an inherited count uses the fixed limit text and names the template in its path (template[<key>].parent). l10n.pack.max_string_bytes bounds every string of a TOML row too (key, template, model, each clear_fields entry, reference and decimal strings), and l10n.pack.max_fields_per_row counts clear_fields entries together with fields.

Staging the same release with the same digest again changes nothing (StageOutcome::Unchanged). The same release id with other content is refused. A new release of the same pack needs a greater pack_version, a release date that is not earlier, and the releases are kept, never replaced.

These parts of ADR 0047 D1 and D7 are follow-up tasks of the pack-format work. A pack that uses them is refused by name, never partly accepted: converted and mixed origins with their NOTICE rule and notice files, the checks of supports contract versions, required capabilities and manifest countries, and the dated lookup by date (it belongs to the rule-binding task).
